rem-se-prior-boundary-control.title: Exact boundary controllability of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation
rem-se-prior-boundary-control.statement: For every $T>0$, endpoints sufficiently near $w(0)$ and $w(T)$ in $H^s(D)$ can be joined by a solution in $C([0,T];H^s(D))$ of the cubic NLS, using full-boundary Dirichlet or Neumann control.
rem-se-prior-boundary-control.hypotheses: $D\subset\mathbb R^n$ is a bounded domain. The nonzero constant $\lambda$ may be complex. A smooth reference solution $w$ exists on $D_1\times(-\eta,T+\eta)$ for a bounded neighborhood $D_1$ containing the closure of $D$, with $\eta>0$. The exponent satisfies $s>n/2$, or $0\le s<n/2$ with $1\le n<2+2s$, or $n=2$ with $s\in\{0,1\}$. Both boundary prescriptions act on the whole boundary; the theorem promises an appropriate control, not a specified common boundary norm.
rem-se-prior-boundary-control.reading_limits: Read the accessible full-paper text extraction of equations (1.1)–(1.3) and Theorem 1.1, printed pp.4129–4131. Fraction bars and some relation glyphs are imperfect in the extraction; the exponent alternatives were checked against the abstract in the same source. rem-se-prior-boundary-control.title: Exact Controllability for the Schrödinger Equation

rem-se-prior-boundary-control.reading_limits: Read the published-paper scan text at printed pp.24–25: equations (1.1) and (1.3), Theorem 1.1, the transposition solution class, and the real inner products at the end of §1. rem-se-prior-boundary-control.locator: §0.1, printed p.6; Theorem 0.1 and equation (0.1), printed p.7; also Numdam archival scan https://www.numdam.org/article/MSMF_1993_2_55__3_0.pdf, PDF pp.5–6
rem-se-prior-boundary-control.statement: For every $T,\varepsilon>0$, plate data $(u_0,u_1)\in(H^{1+\varepsilon}(D)\cap H_0^1(D))\times H^{-1+\varepsilon}(D)$ admit $g\in L^2((0,T)\times\partial D_e)$ such that $u_{tt}+\Delta^2u=0$, $u=0$ on all of $\partial D$, and $\Delta u=g$ on the outer boundary (zero on the obstacle boundaries), with $u=0$ after $T$.

H2 is $\sum_{\gamma\text{ primitive}}\lambda_\gamma d_\gamma e^{\alpha d_\gamma}<\infty$ for some $\alpha>0$, where $d_\gamma$ is the periodic trapped-ray length and $\lambda_\gamma$ is the square root of the product of the two contracting Poincaré eigenvalues.
